newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA T-BILL RATES DECLINE ON C. BANK RATE CUT.
newsitem.headline: MANILA T-BILL RATES DECLINE ON C. BANK RATE CUT.

text.p: Philippine banks were quoting lower secondary bid and offer rates for Treasury bills on Thursday after the central bank slashed its overnight borrowing rate by two percentage points to 18 percent, dealers said.
"The market sentiment is that interest rates will be going down. The peso is starting to stabilise," a trader said.
Banks have started buying bills with yields which are seen to be higher than the projected rates next week, she said.
"But we can't really say yet the peso has normalised since foreign banks have not yet been allowed to participate in the spot market," the trader added.
A Reuters poll of seven financial institutions gave bid rates of 14.45/15.125 percent for the three-month bills; 15/15.875 percent for the six months; and 15.25/16.50 percent for the one-year bills.
The average interbank call loan rate fell to 18.09375 percent from 20.46875 percent in line with the central bank's rate cut.
Volume narrowed to 16.92 billion pesos from 20.20 billion pesos, with 29 lenders and 16 borrowers.
